title: Release audit: `forgel_code/interactive.py`'s `redact()` does not keep key material out of the
summary: Replace `redact()` with a structured redactor that recognizes separators (`:`, `=`, whitespace), auth schemes such as `Bearer`, quoted values, Russian secret labels, environment-variable names and generic key material, and redacts the entire value rather than only the next token. Add direct tests for `token:abc123`, `Authorization: Bearer abc123`, `токен: abc123`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=abc` and an engine reply containing such text.
requirements: Masking means: for a recognized secret-bearing label, the value bound to that label is replaced by a single fixed mask marker while the label is preserved, so the original value does not appear anywhere in the displayed text.
A value following a recognized secret keyword and a colon, with or without intervening whitespace, is masked.
A value following a recognized secret keyword and an equals sign, with or without surrounding whitespace, is masked.
A value following a recognized secret keyword and whitespace (the previously supported single-token form) continues to be masked.
A value that follows a recognized secret keyword plus a colon or whitespace and then an authorization scheme word is masked; the scheme word may remain visible, the credential after it may not.
Secret keywords are recognized in English and in Russian; a Russian secret label followed by a colon, an equals sign or whitespace masks its value exactly as an English label does.
A compound label containing a secret keyword as one of its segments is treated as a secret-bearing label; the whole label may remain visible but its bound value is masked.
Label recognition is case-insensitive, including for non-English labels.
Text not bound to a recognized secret-bearing label is displayed unchanged, including ordinary sentences that merely contain the word for a secret without a bound value.
The label text itself is preserved next to the mask so the user can tell what kind of value was hidden.
Masking is applied to every engine reply and every engine error before it is shown in the session, with no path by which engine output reaches the screen unmasked.
Masking already-masked text neither errors nor reveals a value, and masking empty or secret-free text returns it unchanged.
Previously working session behavior continues to work, including the masking forms that already worked.
acceptance: A message containing a secret label followed directly by a colon and a value is displayed with the value replaced by the mask marker and the value absent from the displayed text.

A message containing a secret label, a colon, an authorization scheme word and a credential is displayed with the label and surrounding wording preserved and the credential replaced by the mask marker.
A message containing a Russian secret label followed by a colon and a value is displayed with the value replaced by the mask marker.
A message containing a compound label built from several segments, one of which is a secret keyword, joined to a value is displayed with the value replaced by the mask marker.
A message containing a secret label joined to a value by an equals sign with no surrounding spaces is displayed with the value replaced by the mask marker.
A message that merely mentions a secret word without binding a value to it is displayed unchanged.
A message with no secret-bearing label is displayed byte-for-byte unchanged, including punctuation, spacing and wording.
Masking the same message twice produces the same displayed result as masking it once, and masking empty text succeeds and yields empty text.
Every engine reply and every engine error that reaches the session display is masked under these rules, with no displayed engine text bypassing masking.
For each recognized form above, the secret value does not appear as a substring anywhere in what the user is shown for that message.
Previously working session behavior does not regress.
plan_goal: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper

external_dependencies.name: Forgel engine command line
external_dependencies.interface: The client starts it as a subprocess with an operation name and reads one JSON object from its standard output, with error text on its standard error; the engine lives in another project and is simulated for the client's own examples.

result.summary: Fixed the two remaining review failures in `redact()` and pinned both forms with executable tests. A quoted value is now masked only between its quotation marks, so the quote characters stay visible for every supported pair and for the bare-label form, and an unclosed quote keeps its opening quote while masking the rest of the line. A run of `:`/`=` separators (spaces included) is now consumed as visible text, so every separator character survives and only the following value is masked. `tests/test_redact.py` gained `test_a_quoted_value_is_masked_between_its_quotes`, `test_every_separator_character_stays_visible` and a one-marker-per-value test, and the existing idempotence test now covers the quoted form and `password==hunter2`. Verified with `python -m pytest -q tests/test_redact.py` (15 tests, 32 subtests, passed) and the full suite `python -m pytest -q` (270 passed, 187 subtests passed).
assumptions: A value that starts with a separator character is not treated as a value, so the bare-label prose rule keeps deciding those cases.
A quoted run is masked strictly between its quotes; for an unclosed quote the rest of the line after the opening quote is masked.

checks.criterion: Separator-bound values are masked whole: 'token:abc123' shows 'token:[redacted]', 'password: hunter2' shows 'password: [redacted]', 'password = hunter2' shows 'password = [redacted]', and 'password==hunter2' shows 'password==[redacted]'.
No other behaviour changes: every behaviour that worked before this change still works afterwards.

review.summary: The attributed change replaces the narrow token-based redactor with a structured label/binding recogniser in forgel_code/interactive.py and rebuilds tests/test_redact.py around the acceptance criteria. Reading the final state against the specification: labels are recognised case-insensitively as single words or '_', '.' and '-' compounds whose segment is a secret word, plus Russian stem-based labels (FR-2); ':' and '=' runs bind and mask a whole value, a quoted run is masked between visible quotes, an authorization scheme word stays visible while the credential after it is masked, a copula is skipped and the following word decides by the stated prose-vocabulary rule, and the marker is never re-masked (FR-1, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-6, FR-7, FR-10). Every pinned example in AC-1 to AC-6 resolves to exactly the stated output (token:abc123, password = hunter2, password==hunter2, Authorization: Bearer abc123, the token Bearer secretvalue, токен: abc123, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=abc, db_password=hunter2, aws.secret.key: hunter2, api-key=hunter2, token abc, токен abc123, the token abc, set password swordfish, password: "hunter2 and more"), and the benign set (Password updated., Secret rotation scheduled, the token is missing, rotate the password please, send the secret later, release: 0.1.1 open, empty text, the Russian sentence) is returned byte-for-byte unchanged because those words are in the fixed prose vocabulary and the empty input short-circuits. Blanket over-masking is the direction the specification explicitly accepts as safe, and the one odd edge I found (a label wrapped in quotes, where the closing quote is read as an opening quote and the rest of the line is masked) is not a pinned form and never leaks a value. The test file maps one-to-one onto the acceptance criteria plus three session-level tests that run real stubbed engines and assert that a reply, a task title and an engine error reach a captured screen with the value absent and the label plus marker present; none of the pre-change scenarios is left uncovered, and the declared 'replaced' names correspond to renamings inside this same attributed change series, with the original scenarios still present and passing. Nothing unrelated, temporary or generated is committed, QA and the acceptance checks pass, and no secret or weakened test is present.

requirements.requirement: A value bound to a recognised secret label is replaced by the single mask marker while the label and surrounding text stay identical.
requirements.note: FR-1: redact() splices only the bound span and keeps everything before and after it unchanged; the marker stays [redacted].

requirements.note: FR-3 and AC-1: token:abc123, password: hunter2, password = hunter2 and password==hunter2 all resolve to the pinned output; the separator run is consumed but emitted verbatim.

requirements.note: FR-5 and AC-2: both Authorization: Bearer abc123 and the token Bearer secretvalue keep the scheme word and mask the credential; the scheme set matches the specified list.

requirements.note: FR-4/AC-6: the quote-pair map masks only the content for double, single, backtick and guillemet quotes and masks to end of line when no closing quote exists.

feedback: Preserve the quotation marks when masking a quoted value: `password: "hunter2 and more"` must render `password: "[redacted]"`. Mask only the characters between the opening and closing quote; the quote characters themselves stay visible. Apply this for every supported quote pair (" ", ' ', ` `, « ») and also for the bare-label quoted form such as `password "hunter2 and more"`; for an unclosed quote keep the opening quote visible and mask the rest of the line.

Preserve every separator character when a label is bound by repeated `:` or `=` characters: `password==hunter2` must render `password==[redacted]`, `token::abc` must render `token::[redacted]`, and the same holds with surrounding spaces (`password = = hunter2` keeps both `=` visible). Concretely, after a label consume the whole run of `:`/`=` characters as visible text and mask only the value that follows.

Make sure tests/test_redact.py in the repository actually contains the tests you cite as replacements: `python -m pytest -q tests/test_redact.py` passed while both forms above are wrong. Commit a test that asserts `password: "hunter2 and more"` -> `password: "[redacted]"` and a test that asserts `password==hunter2` -> `password==[redacted]`, and re-check that masking the quoted result twice leaves it unchanged.
Re-run `python -m pytest -q tests/test_redact.py` and `python -m pytest -q` after the fix and confirm the remaining pinned forms still hold.

last_failure.message: The redactor rewrite handles colon, equals, whitespace, authorization-scheme, Russian, compound and benign-prose forms correctly, and the environment checks pass. Two pinned forms are nevertheless wrong: a quoted value is masked together with its quotation marks (`password: "hunter2 and more"` renders `password: [redacted]` instead of `password: "[redacted]"`), and a repeated separator loses a character (`password==hunter2` renders `password=[redacted]` instead of `password==[redacted]`). Neither form is covered by the attributed tests, and the replacement tests cited in the developer justification are not present in the repository, so the change does not satisfy the quoted-value requirement and does not byte-preserve text outside the masked value for repeated separators.
